RevoZport Ignores the new BMW X5, Launches Tuning Kit for the F95 X5 M
7 photos
Photo: Instagram | revozport
There’s an entirely new BMW X5 out, and in case you somehow missed it, then you should continue to ignore it.
After all, it’s a Neue Klasse model, which means that it looks horrible both inside and out, this writer believes, and just like me, I’m convinced that most petrolheads feel the same. The G65 debuted earlier this year. It hit the assembly line at Spartanburg, in South Carolina, a couple of months ago, and it is also assembled in China, albeit only for the LWB (long wheelbase) that it marketed locally.
The new-gen BMW X5 is based on an updated version of the CLAR platform, so despite the new skin and ultra high-tech interior that will age pretty much like a smartphone, it still shares its nuts and bolts with the G11 7 Series, G15 8 Series, G06 X6, G07 X7, and the XM. The old X5 is also based on the same construction, in case you forgot, and so is its range-topping version, the X5 M, and this story is dedicated to this exact model.
More particularly, it is all about the one pictured above in the gallery, which came directly from RevoZport’s portfolio. The tuner founded more than two decades ago and primarily located in Hong Kong, albeit with operations worldwide, including the United States of America, recently shared images of this modified vehicle on its social media channels, refraining from saying a lot of things about it, and stating it it wears its “street kit.”
Photo: Instagram | revozport The body kit targets the LCI, which is Bimmer slang for facelift and stands for Life Cycle Impulse, version of the F95 BMW X5 M , and makes it look a bit more aggressive. At the front, we can see that this ride features new trim on the side vents, as well as a sharped apron attached to the OEM bumper. The grille surrounds are thicker, so we reckon they have come from RevoZport’s portfolio, too, and so has the hood, with its vented and a lot more aggressive design.
From what we can tell, the wheel arch trim appears to be the same, so there are no fender flares here that would have made the entire thing a bit wider compared to the stock one. The side skirts, on the other hand, have come from the aftermarket world, just like the rear diffuser. The roof-mounted wing looks the same as the OEM element to us, and so does the rear bumper. The door mirror casings also carry over, and the exhaust tips look just as big as the stock ones.
You do know that no tuning job would be complete these days without an aftermarket set of wheels, don’t you? And while we’d like to tell you that the pictured BMW X5 M also ticks this box, we can’t, because the alloys are not fully visible. Thus, we could be looking at the OEM ones, as these are just as big as far as we can tell, though we could be wrong, as they might be new. But do they look like they are part of the tuning job to you?
Photo: Instagram | revozport Before revealing your answer and speaking your mind about this build in the comments box below, we have to tell you that this machine features a satin black look on the outside, and retains its Bimmer roundels at the front and rear, as well as the M logos. The cockpit is not visible at all, though such a thing would look best with black leather upholstery and a few touches of suede here and there, as well as the usual amount of carbon fiber trim.
We cannot tell you whether the engine has been upgraded, but our bet would be on the word “no.” This would mean that the 4.40-liter S68 powering the facelifted iteration of the BMW X5 M , and featuring mild-hybrid assistance, would still develop 617 hp (625 ps/460 kW) at a screaming 6,000 rpm, and 553 pound-feet (750 Nm) of torque between 1,800 and 5,860 rpm. With no outside intervention, this model needs just 3.9 seconds to hit 62 mph (100 kph) from a standstill, and that makes it just a few tenths of a second slower than the iconic Ferrari Enzo.
The performance is definitely something to write home about, because we are talking about a premium mid-size crossover with plenty of space inside. And for what it’s worth, the F95 BMW X5 M, just like the regular G05 X5, have aged like fine wine rather than fine milk, and they are some of the best-looking machines in their class, this writer believes. I want to say the same about the modern-day X5 (and X5 M) a few years from now, but I doubt that it would start growing on me, especially with that soulless interior.
Now, do you dig the makeover of this BMW X5 M , or would you have yours bone stock? I lean on the latter rather than the former, but the tuning job is definitely not bad at all. View this post on Instagram A post shared by RevoZport (@revozportt)
